A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMedPO and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Corresponding content can be matched despite reformatting and table renumbering. Changed experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons but do not prevent comparison of the documents.

before.justification: v1 reports original medical VQA and report-generation experiments on four datasets, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, attention visualizations, and case studies in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and analyses on the four datasets and reports additional baseline comparisons in Table 1 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same hallucinated-response construction, localized lesion noising, multi-LLM relevance scoring, score normalization, and weighted DPO objective. Algorithm 1 and the generation/evaluation prompts are unchanged; the algorithm is relocated.

E1.justification: Both versions use SLAKE and VQA-RAD for medical VQA and IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR for report generation. No dataset, task, or distinct evaluation scenario is added. Revised MIMIC-CXR sample counts change the protocol within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds POVID, SIMA, and FiSAO to both the direct preference-tuning and SFT-based comparisons in Table 1, and to the detailed report-generation comparison. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set beyond DPO, Self-Rewarding, and STLLaVA-Med. The unmodified LLaVA-Med row is also removed from the report-generation ablation table.

E3.justification: Appendix A substantially reduces the reported MIMIC-CXR sample sizes: training pairs per preference type change from 1,600 to 800, total preference pairs from 3,200 to 1,600, and test images/reports from 500 to 200. These are explicit revisions to the documented protocol; neither PDF establishes whether they reflect reruns or corrections.

E4.justification: Section 4.4.2 and Figure 7 lose the hydrocephalus case, retaining the renal-cyst example. The eight Appendix F cases remain unchanged. The principal preference-curation, relevance-weighting, multi-LLM, noise-location, attention, and backbone analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The unchanged five collaboration rounds concern the scoring procedure, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises non-SFT report-generation BLEU values: MMedPO changes from 11.96 to 23.49 on IU-Xray and from 3.52 to 12.85 on MIMIC-CXR. Appendix BLEU components and ablation values also change. Added comparisons introduce new rankings, including FiSAO exceeding MMedPO on SFT IU-Xray METEOR, 35.44 versus 35.17. These are revised reported results; the changed MIMIC-CXR sample sizes preclude interpreting its differences as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The preference formulation, lesion-noising equation, consensus-score calculation, normalization, and weighted objective remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains clinical-aware multimodal preference optimization to improve alignment and factuality. The abstract and introduction retain the claimed 14.2% and 51.7% improvements. Additional baseline evidence does not redefine the stated contribution or claim scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving reduced scoring bias, greater lesion attention, and compatibility with other backbones are retained. The new Impact Statement supplies general deployment and ethical cautions without developing a specific new limitation, failure condition, or mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly states that hyperparameters are held consistent across experiments to avoid tuning bias. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed tuning procedure. Previously documented training settings, scorers, hardware, runtime, prompts, and code-access information remain available.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds works such as AnyPrefer and MJ-Video and removes others including VHELM and LLaVA-Critic. Appendix C adds descriptions of POVID, FiSAO, and SIMA, whose cited works already appeared in v1. The principal positioning around clinical relevance and lesion-focused alignment remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract and several results and case-study passages, shortens subsection headings, adopts author-year citations, and adds an Impact Statement. The main section sequence, appendix organization, and most explanatory prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICML layout, adds running headers, and changes appendix prose from two columns to full width. Algorithm 1, tables, and prompt figures are relocated or resized. Table 1 expands with additional comparator rows and replaces bold/underline ranking marks with colored highlights; appendix tables are reordered, and Figure 7 is reduced to one case. Together these constitute extensive visual reformatting.

improvement.justification: The added baselines strengthen comparative coverage, but v2 introduces unresolved reporting inconsistencies. Its full-method IU-Xray BLEU-1 is 55.36 in Table 7 versus 30.33 in the combined multi-LLM ablation in Table 8; v1's corresponding entries both report 30.33. Section 4.2 retains DPO-based best-baseline comparisons despite stronger added methods, and Table 1 highlights MMedPO's 35.17 as best despite FiSAO's 35.44 on SFT IU-Xray METEOR. The broader evidence and reduced reporting consistency create a tradeoff whose net quality direction cannot be reliably determined from the PDFs.
